options.label: Self – senior multidisciplinary professional
options.description: Default audience for the user: senior engineering, software, AI, architecture, mathematics, and systems background. Be direct and sophisticated without unnecessary beginner-level explanation.

options.label: Self – learning mode
options.description: Use when the user is learning an unfamiliar stack, service, library, domain, or concept and benefits from clear foundations and progressive explanation.

options.label: Self – quick answer
options.description: Use for short, high-signal answers with minimal explanation and no unnecessary side material.

options.label: Self – career / job positioning
options.description: Use for recruiter, hiring-manager, CV, interview, salary, application, or professional-positioning content.

options.label: Self – brainstorming
options.description: Use for exploratory thinking, alternatives, ideas, naming, strategy options, and creative search.

options.label: Self – debugging
options.description: Use for concrete troubleshooting of logs, symptoms, failing code, configuration, or system behavior with minimal unrelated theory.

options.label: Balanced
options.description: Measured and neutral, combining analysis with readable prose without becoming overly terse or overly expansive.

options.label: Analytical
options.description: Logic-first, precise, and structured; distinguish assumptions, evidence, implications, and conceptual differences.

options.label: Direct
options.description: Straight to the result with concrete facts, actions, and conclusions; minimize hedging, padding, and repetition.

options.label: Encouraging
options.description: Supportive and constructive without exaggeration; emphasize practical possibilities and useful next steps.

options.label: Critical-Constructive
options.description: Rigorous judgement: identify concrete weaknesses, explain why they matter, and propose specific improvements.

options.label: Exploratory
options.description: Explore patterns, implications, future paths, alternatives, and conceptual connections without presenting speculation as fact.

options.label: Concise
options.description: Short, high-signal, and structured; keep essential content and remove secondary detail and redundancy.

options.label: Empathetic
options.description: Emotion-aware and respectful, sensitive to personal context while remaining clear and substantive.

options.label: Formal
options.description: Professional, polished, precise, and suitable for official, legal, business, or application communication.

options.label: No explicit depth
options.description: Do not impose a depth preference; let the task and other instructions determine the amount of explanation.

options.label: Overview
options.description: Give the main conclusion and essential context only; avoid edge cases and deep derivations unless required.

options.label: Detailed
options.description: Default working depth: explain important reasoning, context, trade-offs, and practical implications without exhaustive coverage.

options.label: Exhaustive
options.description: Deep review: inspect assumptions, edge cases, alternatives, missing links, and evidence, maximizing useful coverage within practical limits.

options.label: No selection confidence
options.description: Do not add an explicit confidence signal for the selected meta-configuration.

options.label: Low selection confidence
options.description: The selector has weak evidence for the chosen meta-settings; this does not describe factual certainty of the final answer.

options.label: Medium selection confidence
options.description: The selector has reasonable but not decisive evidence for the chosen meta-settings; this is not factual-answer confidence.

options.label: High selection confidence
options.description: The selector has strong evidence for the chosen meta-settings; this does not imply that the final answer itself is factually certain.

options.label: Normal evidence handling
options.description: Use ordinary evidence handling appropriate to the task; no special local-history or external-verification requirement is imposed.

options.label: Local/project/history context first
options.description: Prioritize the supplied project, files, memory, history, code, requirements, and architecture before generic knowledge.

options.label: Strict history + online fact-check
options.description: Use the strongest grounding mode when current, external, non-generic, or explicitly verified facts are required, while respecting relevant local history and project evidence.
